items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 7348acd070f761b5fbbf4804ba19f78577bbb757, which replaces the hand-rolled UTC formatter with a delegation to the shared local-timezone date utility.
items.description: The inline opened-date formatter uses UTC accessors while every sibling date display in this feature area formats through the shared local-timezone date utility, and the companion test file's comment claims local-timezone behavior. For users in non-UTC timezones, a stage opened late in the UTC day displays the next calendar date, disagreeing with every other date shown in the product for timestamps near the UTC midnight boundary.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 7348acd070f761b5fbbf4804ba19f78577bbb757: production switched to the shared local-timezone utility, which keeps the noon-UTC fixture valid, and the test's comment block was rewritten to describe the delegation.
items.description: The opened-date regression test cannot detect a switch between UTC and local date accessors: its fixture is a noon-UTC timestamp, which resolves to the same calendar date in every timezone from UTC-12 through UTC+11, so both accessor families produce identical output and the test passes either way. It provides no protection for its stated intent, and its comment block contradicts the implementation's actual timezone behavior.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 7348acd070f761b5fbbf4804ba19f78577bbb757, which adds a dedicated derivations suite pinning all eight per-stage rules plus the null-for-upcoming and not-applicable invariant.
items.description: The stage-opened-timestamp computation has zero coverage for its single-case derivations: the only opened-at assertion in this spec covers the batch-bypass null case. None of the eight per-stage derivation rules in the change's contract — case creation time, earliest qualifying evidence timestamps, the review-signal timestamp with its fallback, and the downstream entities' creation times — nor the null result for stages not yet reached is pinned by any test.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 7348acd070f761b5fbbf4804ba19f78577bbb757, which pins the batch path's populated opened-at field against the mocked creation time alongside the stripped structural comparison.
items.description: The batch-versus-single parity test was weakened from a direct deep-equality into a strip-and-compare that removes every opened-at key before comparing, a workaround acknowledged in an adjacent comment as masking regressions. The one opened-at field the batch path does populate today can regress silently behind the stripper; a separate pinned assertion on that field closes the hole while the workaround remains.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 7348acd070f761b5fbbf4804ba19f78577bbb757, which renames the test to the should-prefixed form.
items.description: A newly added test name does not follow the should-prefixed naming pattern that the repository's test-authoring rule requires for test titles.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 7348acd070f761b5fbbf4804ba19f78577bbb757, which mirrors the two-row layout in the skeleton with an added placeholder line for the opened-date text.
items.description: The live step row switched to a two-row column layout to fit the opened-date line, but the loading skeleton still renders the old single-row layout, producing a visible layout shift on data arrival for every completed or in-progress step — i.e., every step that carries an opened date.
